title: Choose between Google Gemini tools and structured output
summary: Use this guide to decide whether a Gemini request needs a structured response or an application operation. It also provides recovery actions and verification evidence for each workflow.
prerequisites: A representative request and a written description of its expected result
Access to the application that will validate a response or handle a requested operation

sections.title: Choose the workflow
paragraphs: Which workflow should you use? In this intermediate-level guide, use structured output when the application needs the model response to follow a declared structure. Use tools when the model needs to identify an application-provided operation and supply arguments for the application to handle.

Start by writing the evidence the application needs. If the evidence is data with defined fields, choose structured output. If the evidence is a request to perform or prepare an application operation, choose tools. If the choice remains ambiguous, separate the request into its desired data and desired action, then test each part independently rather than proceeding with an unclear contract.

The cited source changed from content/resources/provider-workflows/google-gemini-tools-structured-output.json, an internal catalogue path with an unregistered publisher and no recorded verification, to the official Google documentation listed in this resource. The change affected source attribution and the workflow distinction: the corrected guidance treats structured responses and application-handled operations as different decisions. Guidance outside that affected scope was not changed.

sections.title: Apply the decision and recover from failure
paragraphs: Step 1: For structured output, declare the response structure using the forms supported by the official documentation, send a representative request, and validate the returned data against that structure. If the request is rejected or validation fails, compare the declaration with the documented supported forms, remove unsupported complexity, and retry with the smallest structure that still represents the required result.

Step 2: For tools, describe the available application operation and the inputs it accepts, then inspect whether the model requests the intended operation with usable arguments. If it requests the wrong operation, omits required arguments, or does not request an operation, make the operation description and input expectations more explicit and retry with a minimal representative request. If the failure continues, preserve the request and response and compare them with the official tool documentation before expanding the test.

Step 3: Keep structural validation separate from checking whether the content is correct for the task. A response can match its declared structure while containing unsuitable values. If that happens, strengthen the request with the missing task constraints and add application-level value checks before accepting the result.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: For structured output, the expected evidence is a response that the application can parse and validate against the declared structure. Verify it with representative normal, boundary, and missing-information requests. If any response cannot be parsed or fails validation, record the failing request, reduce the structure to isolate the unsupported part, and retry only after comparing that part with the official structured-output documentation.

For tools, the expected evidence is a model response that identifies the intended application operation and supplies arguments the application can validate before handling it. Verify that the operation matches the request, required arguments are present, and unacceptable arguments are rejected by the application. If any check fails, do not handle the operation; revise its description or input expectations and repeat the minimal test.

The workflow is verified only when the chosen mechanism produces the expected evidence across the representative tests. If neither workflow does so, return to the decision statement, separate data requirements from operation requirements, and test them independently before combining them in an application flow.
